chiku.ask: After 30 rides, Noor, 20, opens her flashcards as the train leaves. What starts it? Give me one card.

newDay.caption: New day: Noor takes a bus instead, with time and the same wish to study.
newDay.question: Will she open her flashcards as usual?

guesses.why: Your card says the train starts it. The train is gone today.
Your card says the ride count made it stick. The 30 rides are done.
Your card says her wish starts it. She still wants to study.

truth.caption: On the bus, Noor left her flashcards in her pocket.

chiku.ask: Leila, 22, takes a free cafe coin toss that pays $20 or $0. Why does it feel easy to accept? Give me one card.

newDay.caption: New day: The cafe gives Leila a sure $10 first; the toss would leave her with $20 or $0.
newDay.question: Will she take the toss now?

guesses.why: Your card says the sure $10 is her new start. Losing it weighs heavily.
Your card says gaining or losing $10 feels equal. The fair toss still looks fine.
Your card says the new starting point changes nothing. She took this toss before.

truth.caption: Leila kept the sure $10 and passed on the toss.

chiku.ask: At a shop, Maya, 24, raises her desk bid after seeing a $100 tag. Why? Give me one card.

newDay.caption: New day: A random draw shows $100 for another desk; Maya lists two reasons it is too high.
newDay.question: Will she still bid above her earlier $50 plan?

guesses.why: Your card says a first number can still pull her bid, even after she checks it.
Your card says a random number has no pull. She will keep her $50 plan.
Your card says her two reasons erase the pull. She will keep her $50 plan.

truth.caption: Maya offered $55, above her first $50 plan.

chiku.ask: After three late buses, Omar, 21, tests his guess that every bus on his route is late. Why test it? Give me one card.

cards.text: An early bus could disprove it

newDay.caption: New day: A bus arrives early at Omar's stop, after the three late ones.
newDay.question: Will he drop his every-bus-is-late guess?

guesses.why: Your card says one early bus can disprove a claim about every bus.
Your card says one late bus already proved the guess. He keeps it.
Your card says the three late buses proved the guess. He keeps it.

truth.caption: Omar saw the early bus and crossed out his every-bus guess.

chiku.ask: At a station, Eva, 19, checks the platform sign while friends all point to platform 2. Why check? Give me one card.

newDay.caption: New day: The sign clearly says platform 3, but another group still points to platform 2.
newDay.question: Will Eva walk toward platform 3?

guesses.why: Your card says the crowd can be mistaken. Eva follows the clear sign.
Your card says the crowd proves platform 2 is right. Eva stays with it.
Your card says everyone follows the crowd. Eva stays with it.

truth.caption: Eva read platform 3 on the sign and walked there.

chiku.ask: Theo, 20, adds an hour to his poster plan after checking how long his last poster took. Why? Give me one card.

newDay.caption: New day: Theo has another poster to print; last time, the printer line took an hour.
newDay.question: Will he start before his first planned time?

guesses.why: Your card says the last printer line reveals time his first plan missed.
Your card says the smooth plan is normal. He starts at his first planned time.
Your card says past tasks cannot help. He keeps his first planned time.

truth.caption: Theo started an hour early to allow for the printer line.

chiku.ask: After learning new words, Inez, 23, puts her book away and rests before a quiz. Why rest? Give me one card.

newDay.caption: New day: Inez learns another word list, then can sleep or do chores until the quiz.
newDay.question: Will she sleep after studying?

guesses.why: Your card says sleep after learning can reduce forgetting.
Your card says staying up works better. She stays awake.
Your card says busy breaks help more. She does chores instead.

truth.caption: Inez slept after studying, then recalled the new words at the quiz.

chiku.ask: At an arcade, Sam, 18, keeps trying a prize box that pays after changing numbers of tries. Why keep trying? Give me one card.

newDay.caption: New day: Sam feels tired after three empty tries, but the next prize still has no set turn.
newDay.question: Will he try the box again?

guesses.why: Your card says the unknown next prize can keep tries going after empty ones.
Your card says only willpower keeps him going. He feels tired now.
Your card says uneven prizes fade faster than steady ones. The empty tries end his turn.

truth.caption: Sam put in another coin after the three empty tries.

chiku.ask: On campus, Hana, 22, opens her notebook when the 8 a.m. bus arrives, as she planned. What starts it? Give me one card.

cards.text: The named bus is her cue

newDay.caption: New day: The bus is canceled, but Hana has a free hour at home with her notebook.
newDay.question: Will she open it during that hour?

guesses.why: Your card says the bus is her named cue. That cue never comes today.
Your card says her wish is enough. She still wants to write.
Your card says one sharp cue costs nothing. She uses this other free hour.

truth.caption: Hana used the free hour for other tasks and left the notebook shut.

chiku.ask: At a workshop, Zoya, 25, thinks all six classmates noticed her bright shirt, then checks their recall. Why check? Give me one card.

newDay.caption: New day: Zoya wears a bright shirt to another six-person workshop and asks who recalls it.
newDay.question: Will she write 'some noticed' in her notebook?

guesses.why: Your card says her own view can make the shirt seem more noticed than it was.
Your card says everyone noticed it. She writes 'all noticed' instead.
Your card says nobody notices. She writes 'none noticed' instead.

truth.caption: One classmate recalled Zoya's shirt, so she wrote 'some noticed'.
